review_type: AI-assisted assurance review; not independent human TPRM validation
independence_disclosure: Same assistant has prior implementation and baseline exposure; not blinded, external or a replacement for qualified human assurance review.
method: Reasoned reading of all frozen source excerpts, genre/scope/date qualifiers, arithmetic and gold. No evaluator output used to decide source meaning in this review; earlier baseline exposure is disclosed.

cases.rationale: TLS 1.1 < 1.2 on the alternate production endpoint. TLS 1.3 on the primary does not offset that statement.
cases.gold_fact_review: The two enabled-version gold facts and endpoint subjects are supported as unconfirmed source assertions. Neither proves fleet coverage.

citations.quote: Alternate production endpoint 9443: TLS 1.1 is enabled.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Request dated configuration and a protocol-rejection scan for endpoint 9443; investigate the reported below-minimum listener.

cases.rationale: No adverse statement in this excerpt: TLS 1.0 is disabled and TLS 1.2 enabled on edge443.
cases.gold_fact_review: Both local protocol-state facts are supported. Do not infer that TLS 1.1 is rejected, that 1.2 is the only enabled version, or that all endpoints were scanned.
cases.smallest_follow_up: Request missing legacy-version rejection and endpoint coverage evidence only; do not create a failure finding from absent proof.

cases.rationale: Accepting TLS 1.0 connections on port 8443 is a material below-minimum source assertion despite unfamiliar syntax.
cases.gold_fact_review: enabled_version=10 with subject port 8443 is a defensible unconfirmed candidate. The verb accepts supplies activation meaning here, not mere product support.

citations.quote: Traffic on port 8443 still accepts TLS 1.0 connections.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Request a dated handshake scan and configuration for port 8443; target this port rather than resending a generic encryption questionnaire.

cases.rationale: May be enabled during fallback does not establish current activation; it does raise a fallback-path question.
cases.gold_fact_review: No unconditional enabled-version gold fact is justified. Retain the whole conditional statement as uncertainty, not harmlessness or a confirmed failure.

citations.quote: Listener 443: TLS 1.0 may be enabled during fallback.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Ask whether production fallback can activate TLS 1.0 and request its guard/configuration and a fallback test if applicable.

cases.rationale: The 2025-01-10 record is outside the pilot TLS freshness window at 2026-11-01. Preserve the adverse historical assertion without calling it a current exception.
cases.gold_fact_review: enabled_version=10/listener 443 is supported only with the historical source date. The bare triple must not be treated as current production proof.
cases.smallest_follow_up: Request current dated listener configuration or a rejection scan and any evidence of remediation since this record.

cases.rationale: The line-specific test endpoint overrides the document-wide production header for this observation; current production comparison must abstain.
cases.gold_fact_review: enabled_version=10/endpoint 7001 is supported as a test-scoped assertion only. Retain the header-versus-line scope discrepancy.
cases.smallest_follow_up: Confirm whether endpoint 7001 is isolated test infrastructure; request production endpoint evidence rather than assuming this is a production failure.

cases.rationale: Client sessions accepting TLS 1.0 on gateway port 9443 warrant a provisional below-minimum concern.
cases.gold_fact_review: enabled_version=10/gateway port 9443 is supported as an unconfirmed candidate. Gateway identity and service mapping still require verification.

citations.quote: Client sessions on legacy gateway port 9443 accept TLS 1.0.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Request the gateway port 9443 configuration and a dated handshake/rejection scan for that endpoint.

cases.rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.3 coexist on listener 443; the strong protocol does not eliminate the weak enabled protocol.
cases.gold_fact_review: Both gold enabled-version observations are supported for the same listener. Different enabled versions are not inherently conflicting observations.

citations.quote: Listener 443: TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.3 are enabled.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Investigate removal of TLS 1.0 on listener 443 and request a dated scan confirming rejected legacy handshakes.

cases.rationale: Six hours = 360 minutes > 240; two hours = 120 minutes > 60. The explicit exercise exclusion also contradicts full-service testing.
cases.gold_fact_review: All four gold candidates are supported: completed=True, achieved RTO=360, achieved RPO=120 and scope_complete=False. Observed wording ties the measurements to the test; all remain unconfirmed.

citations.quote: Observed RTO 6 hours and RPO 2 hours.
The exercise excluded message broker failover.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Request the executed exercise record and corrective retest covering message-broker failover and the exceeded recovery objectives.

cases.rationale: Target values and future scheduled exercises are planning intent, not achieved operating results.
cases.gold_fact_review: An empty achieved-fact gold list is appropriate. Do not infer completed=True or actual recovery objectives from plan targets, even though the source labels a Test date.

citations.quote: Target RTO 60 minutes. Target RPO 15 minutes.
Exercises are scheduled for next quarter.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Request the latest completed exercise record with actual achieved timings, recovery point, scope and execution date.

cases.rationale: Retain provisional exception/targeted-review attention for the reported five-hour service switch. Do not claim an exact RPO breach from an upper bound; formal RTO measurement semantics also need confirmation.
cases.gold_fact_review: completed=True is supported. Five hours converts to 300 elapsed minutes, but whether switching duration is the defined achieved RTO is not established. Up to ninety minutes denotes <=90, not exact achieved RPO=90; it proves neither >60 nor <=60. Propose qualifying the RTO mapping and replacing the exact RPO gold with an unresolved upper-bound assertion in a separately approved gold version. Do not alter v1.1 now.

citations.quote: Switching the service took five hours, with up to ninety minutes of data loss.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Request the failover start/service-restoration acceptance timestamps and actual recovered data-point timestamps; clarify whether the ninety-minute phrase is an observed maximum or a hypothetical bound.

cases.rationale: The reported achieved 90-minute RTO and 15-minute RPO are within the example limits, but full-service coverage is not established.
cases.gold_fact_review: All three gold facts are supported as unconfirmed results. No scope_complete=True fact is justified, and no whole-control Met follows.

citations.quote: Achieved RTO 90 minutes and RPO 15 minutes.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Request only the missing dependency/coverage record and verify that completion and both measurements belong to the same exercise.

cases.rationale: Not testing identity federation is an explicit exercise scope limitation, warranting review against full-service recovery requirements.
cases.gold_fact_review: completed=True and scope_complete=False are supported as provisional candidates. Confirm that identity federation is a required recovery dependency; the excerpt does not prove the dependency failed.

citations.quote: Identity federation was not tested in this exercise.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Confirm the identity dependency map and request an identity-federation-inclusive exercise result or a justified scope exception for human review.

cases.rationale: Four hours thirty minutes = 270 minutes, exceeding 240 by 30 minutes. Unsupported parser grammar does not make this an abstention in human gold.
cases.gold_fact_review: Both completed=True and achieved_rto_minutes=270 are supported as unconfirmed measured exercise results. RPO and full-service scope are absent, not passing or failed.
cases.smallest_follow_up: Request the executed timing record and corrective RTO retest; ask for missing RPO/coverage evidence only if not already in that record.

cases.rationale: The results concern Orion Data Warehouse, not the assessed Orion Ledger Gateway. They cannot become Gateway exceptions or coverage proof.
cases.gold_fact_review: All three result triples are supported for the Data Warehouse subject only. Their adverse values must stay bound to that different service.

citations.quote: Achieved RTO 300 minutes and RPO 90 minutes.

cases.smallest_follow_up: Request the Gateway exercise record; clarify shared-dependency relevance only if a service mapping supports it.

cases.rationale: The 2024 result is historical despite the 2026 Test date header. No day in 2024 falls within the 365-day interval at 2026-11-01.
cases.gold_fact_review: The 300-minute result is a historical assertion; retain its 2024 qualification and contradictory source context. Completed=True is a separate source assertion, not proof that this metric belongs to a current completed exercise.
cases.smallest_follow_up: Request the current exercise record and reconcile the metric year with the header before relying on the 2026 date.
